scope: New authored fixed-function probes only. No unchanged DeadGears frame, shader, producer or realm gate was rerun. No target DeadGears colour or depth was used to construct either frozen input family.

compiler.scope: Explicit older exploratory Coax compiler, not the current main compiler. New shader and workers emitted once per new input family. Host C uses FP_CONTRACT OFF; remote GCC also uses -ffp-contract=off -fno-fast-math.

shader.effect: Transport 24 authored clip words unchanged from a uniform/storage binding; flat triangle ID 1/2. Fragment output is position.z, position.w, ID, 1. No hand-written shader arithmetic, custom depth, bias, discard, blending or multisampling.
shader.attachments: RGBA32 float plus D32 float, single sample, clear depth 1, strict LESS and writes enabled; both FS position.z and stored D32 words retained.

first_family.freeze: Plan and all three whole-vector predictions existed and were SHA-256 reported before the first GPU execution.
first_family.fixtures: 15 depth-plane cases at three interior samples plus eight two-triangle winner controls: 53 observations/backend. Non-power-of-two w=3/5/7, same/mixed w, constant/varying clip z; exact lattice XY and exact binary barycentric weights. Controls include adjacent-float crossing, exact ties, both separated-depth orders and non-power-of-two crossings.
models: 0: f64(clip.z)/f64(w), f64 linear interpolation, final f32 nearest-even
1: f32(clip.z/w), f64 linear interpolation, final f32 nearest-even
2: f32(clip.z*f32(1/w)), f64 linear interpolation, final f32 nearest-even

first_family.conclusion: All three frozen complete global arithmetic models are rejected on each observed backend. Constant-depth cases alone agree with reciprocal multiplication, but varying planes reject that as a complete model. The analytic w1 adjacent-float contest keeps earlier ID1 at depth0.5 on both GPUs, while every frozen RNE model predicts later ID2. This is not a basis for a production profile, per-pixel model selection, a new depth-error band or a mask.

heldout_coordinate_basis_family.freeze: A separate input-only tool accepts no observation argument. Both complete predicted vectors were frozen and SHA-256 reported before either heldout GPU execution.
heldout_coordinate_basis_family.fixtures: w1; screen triangle (4.5,4.5),(60.5,4.5),(4.5,60.5), z=.125/.875/.375. Baseline plus each vertex axis perturbed by +/-1/1024px retains identical nearest8 coverage vertices. Two crossing controls use fixed front depths .375-/+1/262144 with opposite snapped/original winners; exact tie/separated controls complete 17 cases/43 samples per backend.
heldout_coordinate_basis_family.conclusion: Observed invariance within coverage bins and opposite-winner controls support the existing eight-bit interpolation coordinate basis on these devices. Reject original-coordinate interpolation as a proposed CPU correction. Exact f64/RNE plane arithmetic is separately rejected; neither whole model matches every sample. No universal subpixel/interpolator contract is inferred.

primary_sources_reviewed.fact: Perspective division defines normalized device coordinates as clip components divided by w.
Nonshader viewport/depth representation and operation details are not fixed; the approximate minimum-precision statement supplies no universal four-ULP CPU-plane band.
Triangle data use framebuffer-space barycentric areas; sample z is linearly interpolated. The text does not prescribe the exact measured arithmetic used here.
Abstract rasterization maps clip values through z/w and viewport depth, then interpolates attributes/depth in framebuffer space.
Fragment position.z is rasterization-point depth; position.w is the interpolated reciprocal vertex w.
